milestones.title: Bao'an County founded at Nantou
milestones.detail: The Eastern Jin split Nanhai Commandery and set up Dongguan Commandery; its seat and that of Bao'an County, one of its six counties, stood around modern Nantou.

milestones.title: County seat moves away to Dongguan
milestones.detail: The Tang renamed the county Dongguan and moved its seat to present-day Dongguan city; a military garrison stayed at Nantou.

milestones.title: Nantou and Dapeng walled towns built
milestones.detail: Two garrison towns were walled in the same year as the Ming rebuilt its coastal defences: Nantou, later the county seat, and Dapeng Fortress on the eastern peninsula.

milestones.title: First recorded mention of the name 'Shenzhen'
milestones.detail: The name Shenzhen first appears in a record of 1410; a market town did not form there until the Qing dynasty.
milestones.source: Shenzhen Government Online (深圳地名网), http://www.sz.gov.cn/cn/zjsz/gqgl_1/201009/t20100923_1584673.htm, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenzhen#Toponymy

milestones.title: Xin'an County established
milestones.detail: The southern part of Dongguan County became the separate Xin'an County, with its seat in the walled town of Nantou.

milestones.title: Great Clearance empties the coast
milestones.detail: Between 1661 and 1669 the Qing evacuated the coastal population inland; Xin'an ceased to be a county and much of Nantou was destroyed. The county was restored in 1669.

milestones.title: New Territories leased to Britain
milestones.detail: On 21 April 1898 China leased the New Territories for 99 years. Counting earlier cessions, 1,055.61 of Xin'an County's 3,076 square kilometres passed to British Hong Kong.

milestones.title: Kowloon-Canton Railway reaches Shenzhen
milestones.detail: The Chinese section of the railway opened with Shenzhen station as the last stop on the Chinese side, boosting the market town.

milestones.title: County government moves to Shenzhen town
milestones.detail: The Bao'an County government moved from Nantou to Shenzhen because the town was closer to the railway and had a larger economy.

milestones.title: Bao'an County becomes Shenzhen City
milestones.detail: The renaming was approved by the State Council on 5 March 1979; the Shekou Industrial Zone had been approved on 31 January.

milestones.title: Special Economic Zone created
milestones.detail: In May 1980 Shenzhen was designated China's first special economic zone; the governing regulations were approved on 26 August.

milestones.title: Shenzhen Stock Exchange founded
milestones.detail: The exchange was established in December 1990.

milestones.title: Shenzhen Metro opens
milestones.detail: The first metro lines began operating on 28 December 2004.

milestones.title: Special Economic Zone extended to the whole city
milestones.detail: On 1 July 2010 the State Council dissolved the internal 'second line' border and expanded the SEZ to all districts, a five-fold increase in area.

milestones.title: Summer Universiade
milestones.detail: Shenzhen hosted the 2011 Summer Universiade from 12 to 23 August.

notes: Start date: the modern city dates only from 1979 (Bao'an County renamed Shenzhen City) and the special economic zone from 1980. Under the brief's rule the start is the earliest documented settlement on the city's territory: the founding of Bao'an County in AD 331 with its seat at Nantou, in today's Nanshan District. That date is from the standard histories and is not contested, but it describes a county seat about 20 km west of the place the modern city grew from. Other candidate dates: 1394 (the surviving walled towns of Nantou and Dapeng), 1410 (first record of the name Shenzhen) and 1979. Neolithic sites in the municipality (about 6,700 years old) are not used. Historic core: Shenzhen market town at Dongmen in Luohu, beside the 1911 railway station and the Hong Kong border, is used because the 1980s city spread from there; Nantou Ancient City lies at about 22.545 N, 113.916 E. Population: no pre-1950 figure for Shenzhen town or Nantou was found, so the list is empty and the series starts with the UN data. The sources give only county-wide registration figures for Xin'an/Bao'an County, which then included what is now Hong Kong: 7,608 households and 33,971 people at the county's founding in 1573, and about 18,000 in 1642 and about 4,000 in 1672 according to the 1819 gazetteer (Ng 1983). One source puts Shenzhen's population at 30,000 in 1980. Landmarks: almost everything standing was built after 1980. Skyscrapers are from the CTBUH Skyscraper Center. Left out for lack of a sourced height: Dapeng Fortress gates, Chiwan Tianhou Temple, Chiwan Left Battery, Shenzhen Bay Bridge, and the stadiums.
